newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mar '96 jobs expected to be revised up 90,000.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mar '96 jobs expected to be revised up 90,000.

text.p: The U.S. Labor Department, in a preliminary estimate, said Friday that it expects to make only a slight adjustment to the March 1996 payrolls, revising them up 90,000.
The benchmark revisions are scheduled to be released next June. The department released its preliminary estimate of the revision for the March 1996 reference month in keeping with its usual practice.

Regarding the overall expected revision, Katharine Abraham, commissioner of the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, said, "This is well within the 10-year historical average of plus or minus three-tenths of one percent for benchmark revisions to the establishment survey."
She said it indicated that the monthly sample survey results "tracked closely with the universe employment counts for the 12-month period ending this past March."
Abraham's remarks came with release of the October employment data, which showed the jobless rate remained unchanged at 5.2 percent in October while payroll employment grew by 210,000.
